# clove

> clove is a Clojure interpreter in one C99 file. It runs `.clj` scripts with
> about 8 ms of startup and no JVM, and it can be embedded in a C program or
> bundled with a script into a single native binary. Clojure's semantics are
> the spec: when clove and JVM Clojure disagree, that's a clove bug unless it
> is in the list of deliberate divergences below.

clove is a hobby project written mostly by Claude, and it isn't meant for
critical work. If the code you're writing matters, use JVM Clojure or
babashka. Where clove fits: quick scripts, tools you'll run yourself,
embedding a scripting language in C, and small standalone binaries.

## Using clove from an agent

- `clove file.clj a b` runs a script. Arguments are in `*args*` (a vector)
  and `*command-line-args*` (a list).
- `clove -e '<expr>'` evaluates and prints the last value. It's the quickest
  way to check how something behaves.
- `clove -m my.app` requires `my.app` and calls its `-main`.
- Errors go to stderr as a framed message with the failing form, and the exit
  status is 1. Stdout carries only what the program printed.
- `clove test` runs every `*_test.clj` under the current directory with
  `clojure.test` and exits 1 on any failure.
- `clove judge -a file.clj` fills in `(test expr)` snapshot tests. Files
  need `(require '[judge :refer [test]])` to also run as plain scripts.
- `clove lint file.clj` checks that a file reads, without running it.
- `clove doctor` shows the load path and which libraries it can find.
- `(doc f)`, `(source f)`, `(dir ns)` and `(apropos "str")` work in scripts
  and at the REPL, and are the fastest way to check a function exists here.
- `clove.edn` (bb.edn-style `:paths` and `:tasks`) is read from the current
  directory or a parent. `clove tasks` lists tasks; `clove run <task>` runs one.

## Things that differ from JVM Clojure

- There is no JVM. Java interop is limited to modeled classes and methods:
  `Math/*`, `System/*`, `String` methods, `java.io.File`, `java.time.LocalDate`,
  `Instant`, `java.util` collections, `UUID`, and the common exception
  classes. Don't reach for arbitrary Java libraries; there aren't any.
- Strings index by codepoint, not UTF-16 unit: `(count "𝄞")` is 1.
- Hash maps keep insertion order at every size. Sets don't.
- Syntax quote leaves symbols unqualified: `` `map `` is `map`, not
  `clojure.core/map`. Nested syntax quote doesn't work.
- Float division by zero gives `##Inf`/`##NaN` instead of throwing.
- Namespaces are a flat global with per-namespace aliases. Defs in `user` are
  visible from every namespace. A namespace is its symbol.
- Only `#inst` and `#uuid` tagged literals; other tags are read errors.
- Concurrency is coroutines on one OS thread: `future`, `go`, agents and refs
  all work, but nothing runs in parallel. None of it exists on Windows.
- `#?(:clove ...)` is the reader-conditional feature for clove-specific code.

## Libraries

- Built in: `clojure.string`, `set`, `walk`, `zip`, `edn`, `data`, `math`,
  `pprint`, `test`, `core.async`, `core.match`; plus `clojure.data.json`,
  `cheshire.core`, `babashka.fs`, `babashka.process`, `babashka.cli`,
  `clj-yaml.core`, `medley.core`, and `taoensso.timbre`. Plain `require`.
- clove's own batteries: `json`, `fs`, `process`, `http` (client and
  server), `peg` (parsing expression grammars), `csp`, `libc`.
- Other pure-Clojure libraries: `clove vendor <group/artifact>` or
  `clove vendor <git-url>` copies the source into `./vendor/`, and `clove
  vendor` with no argument resolves `./deps.edn`. Libraries that wrap Java
  won't load.

## Docs

- [Tutorial](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/tutorial.html): the language, by example
- [Coming from Clojure](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/from-clojure.html): what's different, in more detail
- [Scripts and the REPL](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/scripting.html): the CLI, tasks, tests, editors
- [Snapshot tests](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/judge.html): `clove judge`
- [Libraries](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/libraries.html): the load path, vendoring, what runs
- [Standalone binaries](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/binaries.html): `clove bundle`
- [Embedding in C](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/embedding.html): the C API and the GC rules
- [FFI and the JIT](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/ffi.html): calling C from clove
- [Concurrency](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/concurrency.html): futures, core.async, agents, refs
- [Core functions](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/reference.html): every documented name, with arglists
- [Cheat sheet](https://alexalemi.github.io/clove/cheatsheet.html): core functions by topic
